articles.title: How Chili’s Took Control of the Cultural Conversation Again
articles.titleKo: How Chili’s Took Control of the Cultural Conversation Again
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chili’s same-store sales have gained a collective 50 percent over the past three years. So, CMO and EVP George Felix wasn’t dealing in hyperbole when he told investors recently the brand had been “pretty busy.” What Chili’s was up to boils down to a few investment-laden storylines. The company spent $100 million-plus in facilities. It reworked hospitality by pouring back into labor. Chili’s refocused on core execution and menu architecture. But when talking about one of the most-vivid turnarounds in category history, people often start with how loud the brand became. Chili’s in that opening calendar under Felix and CEO Kevin Hochmann—who worked together at Yum! Brands—spent about $32 million in marketing. Three years later, the figure was closer to $132 million. Felix during Brinker’s investor day dove deeper into what’s been the most outward effect of that higher backing: value perception. This chart below, which uses YouGov data, lays out value perception scores among the general population of adults 18–49. Since rerouting, Chili’s result increased by 50 percent, placing it atop the company’s competitive set, widely speaking. However, Felix said, what’s more interesting is the following, which unpacks how value perception turned among customers who saw the brand’s advertising in the past two weeks. Trends were similar. There, too, Chili’s witnessed a sizable increase over the past three years. And again, it topped the competitive field. “But you can see that the increase in value perception is much bigger and the gap between us and competition is much wider,” Felix explained. What that tells Felix, he continued, is Chili’s “Better Than Fast Food” campaign continues to resonate. When customers find the messaging, it makes them think differently about the value Chili’s offers. What gives Chili’s confidence there’s still room to go? “Well,” Felix said, “when you think about ad awareness and the way to think about ad awareness is that is basically asking consumers, ‘have you seen a brand’s advertising in the past two weeks?’” MORE: Chili’s Turnaround Clears Way for New Restaurant Growth How Chili’s Plans to Remain ‘America’s Hottest Restaurant Brand’ For Chili’s, that particular measure hiked roughly 40 percent over the last three years. You’d expect it to, Felix said, when you toss $100 million into the mix. Yet Chili’s, even with such a vivid bump, still trails the largest spenders in its category. “And so that tells me that there are still probably large pieces of the population that have not seen or been exposed to the ‘Better Than Fast Food’ campaign,” Felix said. “And if you look at the last chart, you know that once we do get people to see that, it does change the way that they think about Chili’s.” In plain terms, Chili’s marketing hook has been to reintroduce guests to a brand they might have lapsed on. How they feel about it. What it offers compared to competitors. And then, invest via operations in an experience and environment worth coming back to. That education process, Felix said, remains underway. There’s also the familiar question marketers face—how have holistic metrics translated to sales? Felix pulled up a slide on Chili’s “Five to Drive” categories. Years ago, in 2017, Chili’s slashed 50 menu items and started to refocus on core products. Its offerings had ballooned to 125 items (40 percent cut). That work continued when Hochman arrived, with about 60 percent of the menu getting renovated. Chili’s sliced more than 25 percent of overall items and moved, as Felix said, to what the brand was known for: burgers, crispers, fajitas, margaritas, and now, the Triple Dipper. Meanwhile, Chili’s devised a heavy labor approach where, when 2026 rolled around, the company was investing $160 million more than it did in fiscal 2022. articles.title: Honey Baked Ham Names Kylie Kelce Brand Ambassador and Launches ‘Traditions that Bring Us Home’ Campaign
articles.titleKo: Honey Baked Ham Names Kylie Kelce Brand Ambassador and Launches ‘Traditions that Bring Us Home’ Campaign
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . As brand ambassador, Kelce brings her real-life take on family, food, and hosting to HoneyBaked. The Honey Baked Ham Company today announced Kylie Kelce, podcast host of “Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce” and mom of four, as its brand ambassador and launched “Traditions That Bring Us Home,” a new holiday campaign celebrating how family traditions evolve from one generation to the next. The national campaign runs across TV, streaming, digital, social, and radio now through the holiday season. For generations, HoneyBaked has been part of the moments families look forward to year after year. “Traditions That Bring Us Home” celebrates those moments: the traditions we look forward to, the ways each generation makes them its own, and the people who make them feel like home. For Kelce, that idea is personal. HoneyBaked has been on her family’s holiday table for years, from the signature Bone-In Ham that always makes the menu to the Cinnamon Apples her grandmother, Mimi, loved. After Mimi passed, the family kept serving them in her memory. Today, they’re a favorite with Kelce’s own daughters. “HoneyBaked has been part of my family’s holiday traditions for years, so creating this campaign with a brand I genuinely love was really special,” said Kelce. “The Bone-in Ham is always a centerpiece at our house, and there are certain things you have to have around it: the Double Cheddar Mac & Cheese, the Maple Sweet Potato Souffle, the Rolls, and, of course, the Cinnamon Apples. Those were my Mimi’s favorite, so after she passed, we kept serving them for her. Now all four of my girls love them, even though Wyatt was the only one who got to meet her. I love that something as simple as a favorite food can keep a piece of someone, and a family tradition, going.” As brand ambassador, Kelce brings her real-life take on family, food, and hosting to HoneyBaked. She shows how a new generation is holding onto the traditions it grew up with while creating new ones that fit how families gather today. “We’re incredibly excited to partner with Kylie as our brand ambassador this holiday season and begin this next chapter for HoneyBaked together. Kylie is a natural fit for HoneyBaked. Her connection to our brand is authentic, and she brings a fresh, relatable perspective on how families host and gather today,” said Maegan Markee, Chief Commercial Officer at The Honey Baked Ham Company. “She represents a generation that’s taking the traditions they grew up with and making them their own, which is exactly the spirit of ‘Traditions That Bring Us Home.’ This holiday also marks the start of a broader marketing transformation for HoneyBaked, one that honors our heritage and celebrates our loyalists while finding new ways to connect with the next generation of HoneyBaked customers.” “The best holiday meals aren’t about spending all day in the kitchen, they’re about getting everyone around the table,” said Chef Tim Ziga, Culinary Director at The Honey Baked Ham Company. “HoneyBaked has always made that part easier. Whether it’s a big holiday dinner or a busy night with the family, we want to give people great food and more time to actually enjoy the moment.” HoneyBaked’s holiday menu includes its signature Honey Baked Ham, smoked for up to 24 hours and individually hand-glazed with its sweet and crunchy glaze, along with premium turkey breasts, heat-and-serve sides and desserts. Guests can plan ahead by ordering now at HoneyBaked.com and scheduling in-store pickup closer to Thanksgiving or the holidays. The full menu is available at participating locations nationwide and through HoneyBaked.com. articles.title: Lou Malnati’s to Open in St. Charles, Illinois
articles.titleKo: Lou Malnati’s to Open in St. Charles, Illinois
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Lou Malnati’s Pizzeria announced today that its highly anticipated St. Charles restaurant will officially open Tuesday, October 27 at 3050 E. Main St., further expanding the family-owned company’s presence in the Chicagoland area. The restaurant marks Lou Malnati’s 70th location and will employ approximately 100 team members. The 6,200-square-foot space features a full-service dining room and bar, private dining room, carryout, delivery and catering services. “The St. Charles restaurant represents an exciting milestone in our continued Chicagoland growth,” said Julie Younglove-Webb, CEO of Lou Malnati’s. “Since 1971, we’ve been focused on bringing people together over our handmade deep dish, and we look forward to putting down roots in St. Charles, building lasting relationships and becoming a trusted part of the community for years to come.” “We’re thrilled to welcome Lou Malnati’s to Fox Haven Square and see this highly anticipated addition open its doors,” said Pat Greco, president of G Ninety Family Partners. “Lou’s is an iconic Chicago brand, and we believe the restaurant will be a tremendous addition to both the development and the St. Charles community.” Guests can enjoy the full Lou Malnati’s menu, including its legendary Chicago-style deep dish pizza made with its signature flaky buttercrust, Wisconsin mozzarella cheese and vine-ripened tomato sauce, as well as thin crust pizza, gluten-free options, appetizers, salads, pastas and desserts. The St. Charles restaurant will also be the first Lou Malnati’s location to showcase elements of the company’s refreshed brand experience. Updated visual elements, menu design and interior finishes blend the rich history of the Malnati family with a modern, welcoming atmosphere. To create a restaurant that reflects its new hometown, Lou Malnati’s worked with the St. Charles History Museum to incorporate historic photographs and local storytelling throughout the space. The restaurant design also features family photographs, pizza-pan-inspired décor and subtle nods to the Malnati family’s legacy and Chicago roots. As Lou Malnati’s continues to expand throughout the Chicagoland area, the company remains committed to being more than a restaurant in the communities it serves. Through local partnerships, charitable involvement and genuine hospitality, Lou Malnati’s looks forward to supporting local organizations and becoming an active member of the St. Charles community for generations to come. The restaurant is located in the Fox Haven Square development near the northeast corner of Kirk Road and East Main Street. For more information, please visit loumalnatis.com. The post Lou Malnati’s to Open in St. Charles, Illinois appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Wendy’s Announces $7.99 Dave’s Single Combo Meal
articles.titleKo: Wendy’s Announces $7.99 Dave’s Single Combo Meal
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Wendy’s is putting a square deal on the table. Starting today, customers can score a Dave’s Single combo meal, featuring a Dave’s Single hamburger, small Hot & Crispy Fries, and a small soft drink for just $7.99 – proving fans don’t have to choose between quality and value at Wendy’s. Wendy’s goes the extra mile for each customer, delivering quality food at a price that feels as good as it tastes. The Dave’s Single is a delicious example of that standard. Named after Wendy’s founder, Dave Thomas, the iconic hamburger is made to order with a quarter pound of 100% Fresh, Never Frozen beef*, American cheese, lettuce, tomato, pickle, ketchup, mustard, mayo and onion on a toasted potato bun. WHEN & WHERE: Starting October 19: For a limited time only, fans can order a Dave’s Single combo meal – including a Dave’s Single, small Hot & Crispy Fries and your choice of a small soft drink for just $7.99 at participating U.S. Wendy’s restaurants.** Available to order: In-restaurant, through the drive-thru or via the Wendy’s app and Wendy’s.com . WHY: Wendy’s knows great taste, quality ingredients and exceptional value should go hand in hand. The $7.99 Dave’s Single Combo shines a spotlight on one of Wendy’s most iconic menu items. With roots dating back to the brand’s original five menu offerings, the Dave’s Single has long reflected Wendy’s commitment to serving fresh, quality food without cutting corners. Whether it’s a quick drive-thru visit or dinner for the family, customers can enjoy the Wendy’s quality they love at a price that delivers outstanding value. *Approximate weight before cooking. Fresh beef available in the contiguous U.S. and Alaska, as well as Canada, Mexico, Puerto Rico, the UK, and other select international markets. **Limited time only. U.S. price and participation may vary. Not valid with any other offer or discount. No substitutions. Prices may be higher for delivery. articles.title: The Kolache Factory Makes Birria Kolache Permanent Menu Item
articles.titleKo: The Kolache Factory Makes Birria Kolache Permanent Menu Item
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Birria Kolache is filled with slow-braised birria beef, onions, cilantro, lime and a flavorful consommé, all wrapped in Kolache Factory’s signature dough. The Kolache Factory, the Katy-based bakery-café franchise known for its fresh-baked kolaches, is giving customers what they asked for. After a record-breaking limited-time run, the brand’s Birria Kolache has officially earned a permanent spot on the menu at all Kolache Factory locations. The Birria Kolache was inspired by Erin Hargett of Greenville, South Carolina, who submitted the idea as part of Kolache Factory’s annual Create a Kolache Contest. The customer-created flavor was introduced systemwide as the brand’s April 2026 Flavor of the Month and quickly became Kolache Factory’s No. 1 Flavor of the Month by sales. During its 30-day limited-time run, the Birria Kolache delivered strong systemwide results, including: 43,523 Birria Kolaches sold across all 60 stores 1.8 times the average Flavor of the Month sales per store per day More than 10,000 Birria Kolaches sold per week on average The results made the Birria Kolache Kolache Factory’s No. 1 Flavor of the Month by sales and helped drive the decision to add it to the permanent menu. “The Birria Kolache is exactly what our Create a Kolache Contest is all about,” said Dawn Nielsen, COO of Kolache Factory. “A customer brought us a bold idea and our team brought it to life, and guests responded in a big way. When a limited-time flavor performs like this and customers keep asking for it, we listen.” Priced at $4.98*, the Birria Kolache is filled with slow-braised birria beef, onions, cilantro, lime and a flavorful consommé, all wrapped in Kolache Factory’s signature dough. Unlike traditional birria dishes that are often served with consommé on the side for dipping, Kolache Factory bakes the consommé inside the kolache, creating a portable, flavor-packed version of the popular dish. The permanent menu addition reflects Kolache Factory’s approach to menu innovation, blending global flavors with the brand’s Czech-inspired roots while staying close to what customers want. The brand’s annual Create a Kolache Contest, now in its 8 th year, invites fans to submit original flavor ideas, giving customers a direct role in shaping future menu items. Winning submissions usually get a place on the menu as a limited-time offering. This is the first time a submission has been added to the permanent menu. “Kolache Factory has always been built around approachable, craveable flavors that fit into everyday routines,” Nielsen said. “The Birria Kolache brings something bold and unexpected to the menu, while still staying true to what people love about our kolaches.” The Birria Kolache is now available at all Kolache Factory locations. To learn more or find a location, visit www.kolachefactory.com. *Prices may vary in certain states. articles.title: SIGEP World Heads to Warsaw Ahead of 2027 Trade Show
articles.titleKo: SIGEP World Heads to Warsaw Ahead of 2027 Trade Show
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Data provided by the Italian Trade Agency highlight growing demand in Poland for several food categories of interest to Italian companies. The international journey of SIGEP Meets the World, the Italian Exhibition Group (IEG) roadshow organised in collaboration with the Italian Trade Agency (ITA), continues. Today, 19 October, the initiative stops in Poland at the Embassy of Italy in Warsaw, aiming to strengthen dialogue with the Polish market and create new opportunities for Italian foodservice companies to meet local industry professionals. POLAND: A MARKET OF OPPORTUNITY FOR MADE IN ITALY Data provided by the Italian Trade Agency highlight growing demand in Poland for several food categories of interest to Italian companies: coffee, bread and bakery products, pastry products, chocolate, gelato and other food preparations. In 2025, Polish imports of these products reached €8.22 billion, an increase of 26.1% on the previous year. Over the same period, imports from Italy in these same categories rose to €865.3 million, recording growth of 25.3%. Polish imports of machinery and equipment for food preparation and production also showed a positive trend, pointing to further opportunities for Italian companies specialising in technologies for the sector. WARSAW: THE ROAD TO SIGEP WORLD 2027 The event on 19 October, hosted at the Embassy of Italy in Warsaw and aimed at industry professionals, will provide an opportunity to present SIGEP World 2027, highlighting its main new features, business opportunities and services for international operators. The programme will also feature a roundtable discussion on the outlook and opportunities for foodservice in the Polish market. Moderated by Natalia Aurora Urbanek, editor-in-chief of the trade magazine Mistrz Branży, the discussion will bring together entrepreneurs and experts from the gelato, pastry and Ho.Re.Ca. sectors to explore consumer trends, market developments and the needs of local operators. The meeting will conclude with a networking session, accompanied by a live demonstration and gelato tasting led by Polish master gelato maker Tomasz Szypuła. The Polish stop is therefore offering an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of market dynamics, engage with local operators and showcase the expertise of Italian companies. The event is part of the journey towards SIGEP World 2027 – The World Expo for Foodservice Excellence, scheduled to take place at Rimini Expo Centre from 23 to 27 January 2027. The 48th edition of the exhibition will bring together the pizza, coffee, bread, pastry, chocolate and gelato supply chains, along with the technologies and services driving the sector’s evolution. “Italian gastronomy tells the story of our regions, artisanal know-how and a culture of hospitality that is part of our identity,” says Luca Franchetti Pardo, Italian Ambassador to Poland. “Gelato is one of the most familiar expressions of this heritage, which continues to evolve through creativity and a commitment to quality. We are delighted to welcome SIGEP Meets the World to the Embassy and to share this tradition with Polish professionals, whose talent and experience enrich today’s gathering. A shared passion such as this also deepens mutual understanding and strengthens the economic ties and bonds of friendship between Italy and Poland.” “The Polish market is showing growing interest in Italian foodservice products and solutions, with positive import trends confirming opportunities for our companies, including in professional technologies and equipment,” says Roberto Cafiero, Director of the Italian Trade Agency’s Warsaw Office. “The Warsaw event forms part of the broader collaboration between the Italian Trade Agency and Italian Exhibition Group, aimed at strengthening the international reach of Italian trade fairs and enhancing their role as global platforms for

articles.originalSummary: 글로벌 맥도날드가 개발해 세계 시장에서 검증 받은 대형 버거가 한국에 상륙한다.한국맥도날드는 오는 22일 ‘빅아치(Big Arch)’를 출시한다고 19일 밝혔다. 해당 메뉴는 2024년 포르투갈, 독일, 캐나다에서 초기 테스트를 진행한 이후 여러 글로벌 마켓에서 선보여 왔다.빅아치는 크고 든든한 비프 버거를 원하는 고객 수요와 맞물려 좋은 성적을 거두고 있다. 프랑스에서는 2025년 출시 이후 맥도날드 대형 버거 가운데 판매 1위를 기록했으며 영국과 아일랜드에서는 기간 한정 출시 당시 반응을 바탕으로 2026년 정규 메뉴로 전환됐다
koreanSummary: 글로벌 맥도날드가 개발해 세계 시장에서 검증 받은 대형 버거가 한국에 상륙한다.

articles.titleKo: Les 110 de Taillevent closes its doors
articles.originalSummary: Marylebone restaurant Les 110 de Taillevent is understood to have quietly closed earlier this month. Known for its extensive, French-focused wine selection, the Cavendish Square restaurant offered 110 wines by the glass alongside a list of more than 2,000 bins. Its operating company, Taillevent Operations Limited, formerly known as Taillevent Cavendish Limited, has entered creditors’ voluntary liquidation.

articles.titleKo: Fatburger and Buffalo’s Express Open Co-Branded Unit in Eagle Pass, Texas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . OHG Brands, parent company of Fatburger and Buffalo’s Express , has officially opened a new co-branded location in Eagle Pass, TX. Located at 3777 El Indio Hwy., the new restaurant brings Fatburger’s hand-pressed burgers, fries and hand-scooped milkshakes alongside Buffalo Express’ craveable chicken wings to the community, complete with a convenient drive-thru designed for guests to grab their favorites on the go. Recognized as a Hollywood-favorite, Fatburger has built a reputation for its wide menu variety, including grilled-to-perfection and cooked-to-order burgers, which can be customized with signature toppings including bacon, eggs, chili and onion rings. From Buffalo’s Express, guests can dig into bone-in and boneless chicken wings tossed in a variety of mouthwatering sauces. “Our new Eagle Pass drive-thru location provides added convenience and flexibility, allowing us to serve both local residents and the many travelers passing through Eagle Pass,” said Jake Berchtold, COO of OHG Brands’ Fast Casual Division. “We’re excited to open our doors and deliver the quality, flavor and hospitality our fans know and love.” “We’re incredibly excited to open our doors and welcome the Eagle Pass community,” said the De Los Santos family, franchise owners of the Fatburger and Buffalo’s Express Eagle Pass location. “We look forward to creating a place where families and friends can come together and enjoy the Fatburger experience.” The new Fatburger and Buffalo’s Express is located at 3777 El Indio Hwy. in Eagle Pass, TX, and is open Sunday through Thursday from 11 a.m. to 10:30 p.m., and Friday through Saturday from 11 a.m. to 11:30 p.m. For more information on Fatburger and Buffalo’s Express, visit www.fatburger.com. articles.title: Le Colonial Delray Beach Expands Group Dining With New Menus and Experiences
articles.titleKo: Le Colonial Delray Beach Expands Group Dining With New Menus and Experiences
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Le Colonial Delray Beach, the acclaimed French-Vietnamese restaurant inspired by the elegance of 1920s Saigon, has unveiled new private dining and catering menus, expanding its offerings for intimate dinners, corporate gatherings, holiday parties and other special events, just in time for the holidays. Private dining options include The Parrot Room, an intimate private dining room for up to 12 guests; The Lounge, accommodating up to 40 seated or 80 standing with its own private bar; the lush, covered Outdoor Patio, hosting up to 70 guests; or the Main Dining Room, which seats 80 and is available for exclusive buyouts upon request. Private events feature Le Colonial’s signature family-style dining experience, with customizable three-course and four-course menus, as well as the Le Colonial 1993 tasting experience. Lunch packages begin at $65 per guest, while dinner packages start at $100 per guest. Dietary accommodations, including halal offerings with advance notice, are also available. For gatherings beyond the restaurant, Le Colonial has also introduced new catering menus for groups of 10 to 45 guests. The catering program features customizable à la carte selections and family-style packages showcasing favorites such as Vietnamese rolls, Heritage Pork Ribs, Chicken Curry, Roasted Salmon, Shaking Beef and Signature Fried Rice. Signature packages, including The Le Colonial Table and the Golden Saigon Package, offer curated selections of appetizers, entrées, sides and desserts for effortless entertaining. Whether hosting an executive dinner, milestone celebration, wedding event, holiday party or catered gathering, Le Colonial Delray Beach pairs timeless ambiance, exceptional cuisine and gracious hospitality to create memorable experiences both in the restaurant and beyond. articles.title: Captain D’s Eyes Growth in Europe
articles.titleKo: Captain D’s Eyes Growth in Europe
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Captain D’s, the leading fast-casual seafood franchise in the United States, is building momentum for international growth as interest from prospective franchise partners expands across Europe. Following a successful international development trip earlier this year, Senior Vice President of International Operations and Development Hair Parra will return to Europe in October to meet with prospective franchisees and explore opportunities in additional markets. The trip is tentatively planned for the second week of October and is expected to include Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom, with additional markets potentially added. Interest in Italy has been particularly active, with Captain D’s currently in conversations with prospective partners. The company is also exploring opportunities in Spain, including Madrid and Valencia, while Poland and France remain markets of interest. “Every time we travel internationally, we come home with more conversations and more new relationships,” said Parra. “It’s exciting to get meaningful interest from experienced operators who recognize the opportunity in bringing a proven American seafood brand to their markets.” The international momentum comes as Captain D’s enters a new phase of U.S. growth, highlighted by the September unveiling of its new restaurant design in San Antonio, Texas. The location is the first U.S. showcase for a refreshed experience, featuring a contemporary design and more inviting guest environment while maintaining the brand’s familiar identity. Captain D’s plans to introduce the new design in additional U.S. markets, including Florida, Ohio and Oklahoma, while continuing to pursue qualified international partners. “Our growth story is bigger than opening individual restaurants,” said Brad Reed, Chief Development Officer for Captain D’s. “We’re evolving the Captain D’s experience while staying true to what has made the brand successful for more than five decades. That combination is creating interest from operators who want to be part of the next chapter of Captain D’s, both here in the U.S. and internationally.” Captain D’s is seeking experienced restaurant operators, multi-unit franchisees and master franchise partners interested in developing multiple locations internationally. Prospective partners can contact franchising@captainds.com. The post Captain D’s Eyes Growth in Europe appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: TGI Fridays Crowns World’s Best Bartender Amid Global Comeback
articles.titleKo: TGI Fridays Crowns World’s Best Bartender Amid Global Comeback
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . TGI Fridays, where the world goes to celebrate, brought together eight of the brand’s best bartenders from across the world to compete in the 29 th World Bartender Championship (WBC), a flagship event at its Global Business Conference in Orlando. During a week focused on global brand momentum, the friendly competition between TGI Fridays’ most skilled bartenders really brought the spirit of the brand to life. Bartenders representing Japan, Greece, the UK, USA, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, Taiwan, and the Philippines showcased their bottle-spinning skills, with the crown going to Roniel Lopez from TGI Fridays, Manila. The contestants were judged by an expert panel on a combination of technical precision, brand knowledge, speed, and showmanship, while displaying the freestyle flair, personality, and lively personality that is synonymous with TGI Fridays. “It was a privilege to enjoy the skills and technical craft shown by the finalists, and I couldn’t be prouder of the eight experts who competed. Congratulations to Roniel on an impressive performance, and we hope visitors to our Manila restaurant enjoy seeing him in action” said Ray Blanchette, CEO, TGI Fridays. “The Global Business Conference was the perfect setting to bring the WBC back and give attendees an opportunity to show their support for colleagues and enjoy such an integral part of Fridays history.” TGI Fridays Global Business Conference saw brand leaders, franchisees and team members from more than 40 countries come together to discuss the global momentum of Fridays “1-2-3 Strategic Vision,” a growth plan to surpass 1,000 units and $2 billion in annual revenue by 2030. Under the theme “Fridays United,” the conference celebrated the company’s ongoing domestic and international resurgence. Fridays leaders took part in educational sessions and an interactive peer-driven Q&A panel on how regions tailor local strategies while staying true to global brand standards. They also heard from the teams behind several notable 2026 milestones, including the company’s first U.S. development agreement in more than a decade and entry into new territories that includes Pakistan, the Balkans, and Sub-Saharan Africa. “Working in the hospitality industry opens a world of opportunities, and TGI Fridays believes it is the responsibility of every team member to demonstrate their commitment to improving how we show hospitality to our guests,” said Phil Broad, Global President, TGI Fridays International. “Fridays United is an ethos that reflects the culture and mindset we are embracing globally across the brand, centered on collaboration, continuous improvement, and a commitment to making TGI Fridays our guests’ favorite choice. That spirit was on full display at our Global Business Conference that saw our leaders come together to share ideas, learn, and celebrate the future of the brand.” To learn more about TGI Fridays franchise opportunities, please visit www. tgifridays.com/franchise/. articles.title: Baccarat Hotel New York Names New Executive Chef and Head Sommelier
articles.titleKo: Baccarat Hotel New York Names New Executive Chef and Head Sommelier
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Baccarat Hotel New York , the Forbes Five Star AAA and Five Diamond hotel, announces the appointment of two food and beverage team leaders at the award-winning property. Chef Isaac Olivo has been named the Executive Chef, and In this role, he will collaborate with Chef Gabriel Kreuther, the hotel’s Two Michelin-starred Culinary Director in overseeing all food and beverage operations. This includes the Grand Salon, The Bar and Le Jardin, private events, and in-room dining. Beata Parzych is the new Head Sommelier, where she will oversee the entire wine program at the flagship property which includes the Grand Salon, The Bar, in-room dining, private bar service, and catered events. Chef Olivo brings nearly 20 years of culinary experience to this new position, having worked at world-renowned kitchens around the country and under acclaimed chefs. His previous work experience includes Executive Chef roles at two esteemed Relais & Châteaux establishments; Cuvee Restaurant at The Chatham Inn in Chatham, MA, and the Mayflower Inn & Spa in Washington, CT. Chef Olivo also held culinary leadership positions at Amorette Restaurant in Lancaster, PA, and Restaurant Clement in The Peninsula, New York. He began his career as a Sous Chef at Bourbon Steak by Michael Mina in Miami, FL, and his work experience includes tenure at SHO by Sean Hergatt in NYC, The Villa by Barton G in Miami Beach, and Jean Georges in NYC. A New York City native of Dominican heritage, Chef Olivo earned a Culinary Arts Diploma from Le Cordon Bleu and brings passion, creativity, and refined technique to the kitchen. Inspired by his father and grandmother, he discovered his love for cooking at an early age. Known for his seasonal, sustainable approach, Chef Olivo blends French technique with contemporary American flavors while honoring craftsmanship, culture and mentorship. He has also represented Relais & Châteaux at international events such as World Oceans Day, advocating for sustainability and ocean conservation. “I am thrilled to be part of something shaped by a pedigree rooted in centuries of excellence, craftsmanship, and an appreciation for the art of living well, and my goal is to bring this spirit to the table,” says Chef Olivo. “Baccarat Hotel New York is a celebration of joie de vivre which honors tradition while also embracing the inventiveness of today’s modern culinary landscape and for me it is all about creating cuisine that feels both timeless and contemporary at this sparkling property,” he adds. With nearly 20 years of experience in fine dining and luxury hospitality, Beata’s brings her expertise in wine, exceptional service, and the art of creating memorable guest experiences to her new role. Prior to joining the hotel, she worked at a variety of premier Michelin-starred establishments in New York City, including Le Bernardin, and Le Cirque and Circo Restaurants. Beata also held beverage leadership and sommelier positions at BLT Restaurant Group, STK Saint Urban, Rhubard Hospitality Collection, STK, and Zuma, all in the city. “In my new role I am excited to bring together my passion for continually evolving within the world of wine and hospitality, with a thoughtful, guest-focused approach to leadership, “ says Beata. “My focus is on maintaining high standards while building a collaborative team culture, while ensuring that knowledge, consistency, and genuine hospitality come together in every guest interaction,” she adds. articles.titleKo: Snarf’s Sandwiches Expands in Dallas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Snarf’s Sandwiches, the family-owned sandwich brand known for its oven-toasted subs, premium ingredients and anything-but-ordinary personality, is continuing its expansion in Dallas and the surrounding area. With six locations now serving the Dallas area, including a new location that opened last week at Preston and Belt Line (14999 Preston Rd., Ste 226, Dallas 75254), Snarf’s is building a growing following among North Texas diners looking for a sandwich experience that stands apart from the ordinary. Founded in Boulder, Colorado in 1996 by Jimmy “Snarf” Seidel, Snarf’s was born from a simple ambition: create the world’s finest sandwich. The company expects additional agreements to be announced in the coming weeks. Its preliminary domestic development outlook calls for approximately 20 restaurant openings over the next two to three years. That would represent an important reversal for a chain that has spent several years contracting. TGI Fridays shuttered a net of U.S. 212 restaurants between 2023 and 2025, leaving 69 franchised U.S. locations, according to the company’s website. Its global footprint stands at nearly 400 restaurants. The renewed domestic expansion effort is part of TGI Fridays’ 1-2-3 Strategic Vision, which calls for more than 1,000 restaurants and $2 billion in annual revenue by 2030. However, Kirkley says the company is being deliberate in how it recruits franchisees and structures development commitments. Most prospective agreements involve five to 10 restaurants, with provisions allowing operators to expand their territories if their initial locations perform successfully. The company is also evaluating nontraditional opportunities in hotels, airports, and travel stations. “The biggest thing for us is franchise health. So making sure that the franchisees that we are currently signing on feel comfortable with the deal as well as the opportunity in the areas that they’re in,” Kirkley says. The Bliss Bites agreement brings TGI Fridays back to its roots in New York, where the brand opened its first restaurant on Manhattan’s Upper East Side in 1965. Chand is a hospitality veteran with more than 35 years of experience. His existing business interests include hotels and other properties throughout New York. Kirkley first met Chand in January, when the two had lunch at a TGI Fridays location on Long Island. She says he was drawn to the company’s work to improve its core menu and restore the hospitality experience associated with the brand. But the decision to move forward involved more than his financial qualifications and development experience. Kirkley visited one of Chand’s newly opened hotels and stayed overnight without informing him she would be there. The New York agreement could eventually expand geographically. Five Guys, Connor Schell’s Full Day Productions, a Words + Pictures company, and Lost Tribe Creative, today released a five-episode docuseries entitled On The Line: The World Burger Games on Prime Video. Produced by Full Day Productions, a premium sports and entertainment studio, in collaboration with Lost Tribe Creative, On The Line takes viewers from local qualifying rounds around the world to the ultimate Five Guys Games championship, capturing the personalities and pressure behind one of the brand’s most celebrated traditions. The series is showrun by Collin Orcutt ( Any Given Saturday, Omnivore ). The finale was hosted by Charissa Thompson, who interviewed competitors before and after each event. The Five Guys Games started in 2013, as a Murrell family idea to celebrate hardworking Five Guys crew members. This year, the games drew participants from stores around the world competing in three events – the potato race, cheese race and dressing/QC race, with each contest demanding a level up on the skills that go into every Five Guys order. “The games began as a thank you to the people who make Five Guys what it is,” Five Guys Founder Jerry Murrell said. “Now, I’m watching crews from across the world compete on a brand new stage. I honestly don’t have words for it.” “With On The Line: The World Burger Games , we saw an opportunity to tell a story that goes far beyond competition,” Full Day Productions President David Chamberlin said. “At its heart, this series is about the people who bring Five Guys to life every day; their pride, dedication, camaraderie and the incredible culture they’ve built across the globe. We’re proud to partner with Five Guys and Lost Tribe Creative on this intimate, character-driven look at a tradition that celebrates the people behind the brand in an authentic and entertaining way.” Spoiler Alert: We Have a Winner, Folks The 2026 Five Guys Games concluded May 13 at The Theater at MGM National Harbor in Maryland, where Jonathan Martinez, of Poughkeepsie, New York – known to fans as “The Terminator” – defeated past champions to claim the title and championship belt. On The Line: The World Burger Games captures the sweat and sacrifice of crew members as they chase a shot at the grand prize – a $100,000 check. Lost Tribe CEO Jason Saffran said being a part of the evolution of the Five Guys Games, from a small contest on a trade show floor to today’s global competition, has been inspiring. “We have always been inspired by the level of intensity and pride each competitor brings,” Saffran said. “The opportunity to share these crew members’ journeys from their homes around the world to the big stage has been as profound and electrifying as the games themselves.” The Five Guys Games are open to any Five Guys employee. On a warm fall morning in October, Freddy’s leadership whipped out big red scissors and a long piece of ribbon to mark the opening of the brand’s first location in Beaufort, South Carolina. But in the background of this moment, with staff members and C-suite executives gathered together, there were three golden balloons shaped as numerals to showcase an important milestone—Freddy’s has reached 600 units systemwide. It marks a significant achievement for a brand that began in Wichita, Kansas, in 2002. But the new restaurant represents more than another addition to the chain’s national footprint. It offers a glimpse into how Freddy’s plans to accelerate expansion as development becomes more expensive and operators face continued pressure on profitability. The unit introduces a 2,300-square-foot endcap format without a drive-thru. Operated by longtime franchisee Charleston Custard, the location seats 65 guests and includes an outdoor patio. The format is part of a change in Freddy’s real estate strategy. Historically, opening a restaurant typically required purchasing land and constructing a freestanding building. The company is now giving franchisees more opportunities to lease existing spaces, reducing upfront costs and opening markets that previously would have been difficult to develop. “Six years ago, Freddy’s was a franchise opportunity for folks who could afford to buy an acre of land and build a building, and that’s a very meaningful investment,” CEO Chris Dull says. “Whereas, today, with a format like this restaurant, you don’t have to buy an acre of land, you don’t have to build a building. You have to finish out an interior, bringing that investment level meaningfully down.” The prototype is smaller, but still maintains Freddy’s historical branding. Freddy’s places a major emphasis on hospitality at the counter. The strategy is already changing Freddy’s development pipeline. Chief development officer Andrew Thengvall says approximately half of the company’s current pipeline consists of endcap, inline, or second-generation restaurant spaces. Just a year ago, those formats represented approximately 10–15 percent. The company has also identified savings through changes to restaurant construction and equipment procurement. Thengvall says recent projects have eliminated $200,000–$300,000 in building costs without materially changing the customer experience. “It’s quicker to open. It’s a lower investment, and frankly, it’s easier to operate,” Thengvall says. Freddy’s has been testing smaller formats for several years. Of the approximately 40 corporate restaurants it operates, the six most recently developed locations have used non-ground-up formats. The company also has more than 50 franchised restaurants in non-freestanding buildings. The smaller restaurants also create opportunities in denser trade areas. Freddy’s historically developed many locations on the outskirts of growing communities, where land was more affordable. Leasing existing retail space allows the brand to pursue established urban and suburban locations without purchasing expensive parcels. “The landscape of opportunities for us is 10x what it was just a few years ago,” Dull says. Big Development Pipeline Freddy’s is the 14th-largest burger chain in America, earning $1.04 billion in U.S. systemwide sales last year. It opened a net of 124 restaurants across 2023, 2024, and 2025. The chain expects to open approximately 60 restaurants in 2026, continuing a steady pace of annual expansion. The company has more than 450 restaurant commitments in its development backlog and approximately 80 franchise operating groups. Its pipeline spans the country, with activity in Washington, California, Florida, South Carolina, and the Philadelphia area, among other markets. A new chapter in Perkins history begins Oct. 19, when Perkins Griddle & Go opens its first U.S. location in Flemington, New Jersey. The milestone marks the highly anticipated U.S. debut of Perkins next-generation fast-casual concept and the brand’s return to the Garden State, led by local franchisees Giuseppe and Nicole Lahara. Blending more than 65 years of Perkins heritage with a modern approach to convenience, Perkins Griddle & Go brings the familiar flavors guests know and love into a fast casual experience designed for today’s busy lifestyles. From breakfast on the way to work to a satisfying lunch, dinner or an afternoon bakery treat, the new concept makes it easier than ever for guests to enjoy Perkins throughout the day. “Bringing Perkins Griddle & Go to New Jersey is an incredibly exciting milestone for our company,” said Matt Carpenter, President of Perkins Restaurant and Bakery. “We’re taking everything people have loved about Perkins for generations and bringing it to life in a completely new way. Flemington is where this next chapter begins, and we’re excited to welcome guests back to Perkins while introducing a new generation to the brand.” For the Laharas, the opening represents more than a new business venture. Longtime Perkins fans and New Jersey residents, the couple is bringing a brand they have loved for years back to their home state while building a family business they hope will become a lasting legacy for their four children. The Flemington café is the first of 16 Perkins Griddle & Go locations the Laharas have committed to developing across New Jersey, following the expansion of their original 10-unit franchise agreement to include additional locations in Monmouth and Ocean counties. “Nicole and I have always loved Perkins, so the opportunity to bring the brand back to New Jersey and be part of its next chapter means a great deal to our family,” said Giuseppe Lahara, franchisee of Perkins Griddle & Go. “We’re building something our children can one day grow into and carry forward as part of our legacy.” A Fresh Take on a Perkins Favorite Designed to meet the needs of today’s consumers without losing the comfort and hospitality that have defined Perkins for decades, Griddle & Go offers a streamlined, fast-casual experience with the flexibility to fit any occasion. After placing their order at the counter or self-service kiosks, guests can grab a quick bite or settle into the café-style dining room for a more leisurely visit. The concept brings together the best of Perkins signature menu with new offerings created specifically for the fast-casual format, including a Pork Roll sandwich and breakfast burrito. Guests can look forward to classic breakfast favorites, alongside specialty Griddle Greats, made-to-order breakfast sandwiches, lighter fare, burgers and sandwiches. The menu also features the bakery treats that have made Perkins a household name, including its iconic Mammoth Muffins, cinnamon rolls, cookies, brownies and signature pies. With breakfast, lunch and dinner options available throughout the day, Griddle & Go delivers the variety and value of Perkins in a convenient new format. Its modern design, compact footprint and flexible service model make it an exciting addition to the brand’s portfolio, creating new opportunities to bring Perkins to more communities. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The partners look for acquisitions where they can preserve what an existing operator built and identify areas for improvement. Matthew Keiser and Brad Paxton didn’t come to Taco John’s through the traditional restaurant career path. They came from medical sales, looking for a business that could diversify their income. Nearly a decade later, that side venture has become their full-time business, spanning 22 Taco John’s restaurants across eight states and giving the longtime business partners a platform for further expansion. Keiser grew up in western Nebraska, part of Taco John’s core Upper Midwest territory. Paxton came from Paducah, Kentucky, another longtime market for the brand. Their familiarity with the chain eventually turned into a business idea. “We kind of started talking about it, saying like, ‘Man, we loved it. We miss it.’ And we were like, let’s see if we can add more Taco John’s to the world and bring them out further than where they’ve been,” Keiser says. They began operating two restaurants in central Kentucky and quickly discovered restaurant ownership demanded more attention than a secondary venture could receive. The partners eventually sold their medical sales business and committed full time to restaurants. Their expansion since then has come primarily through acquisitions. Of the 22 Taco John’s restaurants in their portfolio, Keiser and Paxton built two and acquired the rest. Taco John’s long history has created a pipeline of longtime franchisees reaching retirement or seeking an exit, giving the pair opportunities to acquire established restaurants with proven sales and experienced teams. The partners look for acquisitions where they can preserve what an existing operator built and identify areas for improvement. AUV and the strength of the restaurant’s general manager are two major considerations. New development is evaluated partly on whether another restaurant can fill geographic gaps and make existing operations easier to support. As the portfolio grew, they promoted experienced Taco John’s employees into multi-unit roles and gave general managers additional responsibility. Stores communicate through back-office platforms, participate in speed-of-service competitions, share ideas, and recognize wins across the organization. “Even though you’re hundreds of miles away, it doesn’t really feel that way with our organization because they’re so tight knit,” Paxton says. Their learning curve stretched far past geography. Moving from medical sales into restaurants introduced them to a business where small changes in food and labor costs could carry significant consequences. Paxton says their existing back-office operation helped with the transition, but experienced employees taught them how to monitor controllables, labor, and food costs. Their first opening supplied another lesson. Sales initially struggled, forcing the partners to find unconventional ways to create awareness. Keiser attached his own sign to a Department of Transportation sign near the restaurant and got in trouble for it. “If you think you’ve done enough, you probably still need to do more,” Keiser says. articles.title: The Hidden Cost of Losing Your Cool as a Restaurant Leader
articles.titleKo: The Hidden Cost of Losing Your Cool as a Restaurant Leader
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Poised leaders recognize when they have become fragmented. They acknowledge the effect of their behavior. During my years as a multi-unit Cold Stone Creamery franchisee, I learned that some of the most important leadership lessons do not arrive in classrooms, conference rooms, or carefully planned training sessions. Sometimes, they explode in a parking lot. My wife and I were operating multiple Cold Stone Creamery locations, and the demands of restaurant ownership followed us everywhere. Operations, payroll, employee training, customer complaints, inventory, staffing, and the countless unexpected problems of running restaurants all competed for our attention. After an especially busy Friday night, I arrived at the store Saturday morning already tired and overwhelmed. The crew was moving quickly to prepare for the day—making ice cream, filling the mix-ins, baking waffle cones, and getting ready for customers. My wife arrived in our SUV with supplies for the store. Several employees and I went out to help unload. When the rear hatch opened, a gallon of milk fell from the vehicle. It hit the pavement, burst open, and splashed milk across the asphalt, our shoes, and everyone’s legs. I lost my composure. Instead of accepting the accident and helping address it, I kicked what remained of the first gallon across the asphalt. I then reached into the SUV, grabbed the second gallon of milk, and threw it across the parking lot. Then everything became quiet. No one said a word. My employees stared at me in disbelief. Their expressions communicated what they did not need to say: What just happened? Is this really our leader? In that silence, I saw myself through the eyes of the people I was supposed to be leading. The first gallon was an accident. I could not stop it from falling. But I could have prevented the second. That distinction has stayed with me because it captures one of the most important challenges in restaurant leadership. We cannot prevent every disruption. We cannot control every callout, late delivery, equipment failure, guest complaint, employee mistake, or gallon of milk that falls from a vehicle. However, we are responsible for what we add to the moment. The first gallon created a mess in the parking lot. My reaction created a second mess in the culture. The Human Moments Behind Restaurant Performance Restaurant managers deal with staffing shortages, narrow margins, variable demand, guest expectations, technology disruptions, and time constraints. They make decisions rapidly, repeatedly, and visibly. Most restaurant organizations prepare managers to execute procedures. They teach food safety, labor management, inventory control, guest recovery, cash handling, and operating standards. Those systems are essential. But procedures cannot anticipate every human moment. A procedure cannot determine the tone a manager uses when an employee makes a mistake. It cannot prevent frustration from becoming intimidation. It cannot decide whether a manager responds to a callout with curiosity or condemnation. It cannot repair trust after a leader’s reaction damages it. Those moments require something beyond operational competence. They require leadership alignment. I knew how I wanted to lead. I understood the importance of treating employees with respect, maintaining composure, and setting the emotional tone for the operation. My problem was not a lack of knowledge. It was a lack of alignment. What I believed, how I wanted to relate to my employees, and how I actually behaved had pulled apart. The leader I intended to be and the leader my employees experienced were not the same person. That is fragmentation, which is the gap between intention and behavior. Pressure did not create that fragmentation. It exposed it. Leaders Transmit More Than Instructions A manager’s emotional state rarely remains contained within the

articles.title: Longtime Captain D’s Guest Wins Cruise Trip to Alaska
articles.titleKo: Longtime Captain D’s Guest Wins Cruise Trip to Alaska
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Sandra Elmore has been going to Captain D’s since the Scottsboro store opened in the late 1970s. Captain D’s , the nation’s leading fast-casual seafood restaurant, has surprised a Scottsboro, Alabama, woman with the trip of a lifetime – a family cruise to Alaska! Sandra Elmore has been going to Captain D’s since the Scottsboro store opened in the late 1970s. This summer while she was there for her favorite fish dinner, she noticed a promotional sign for the “Captain D’s and PepsiCo Alaska Family Cruise Sweepstakes,” promoting the chain’s wild caught fish from Alaska. She scanned the QR code, submitted her receipt and forgot all about it. Weeks later when she received an email saying she was the winner, she was skeptical until she received the paperwork and a 32-pound box of cruise-themed merchandise from Captain D’s. They sent six sets of spa robes and slippers, binoculars, beach towels, loads of Captain D’s swag, and of course, Captain D’s gift cards. “We are just astonished and grateful,” Elmore said. “We have always loved Captain D’s, but this is just so over and above. Words fail me. I never expected it, but we’re very excited!” More than 5,000 Captain D’s fans entered the five-week promotion before a winner and five guests were selected to win a seven-night Alaska cruise, three ocean-view rooms, roundtrip airfare to Seattle, two nights of hotel accommodations in Seattle and a $3,000 travel stipend. Captain D’s launched its Wild Caught Batter Dipped Fish from Alaska nationwide in June as part of the brand’s continued focus on high quality seafood sourced from the United States. The fish comes from the cold waters of Alaska and is hand-battered fresh daily in Captain D’s restaurants. The Alaska cruise was a way to give guests the opportunity to experience the place where the brand’s fish is sourced. “The Alaska Family Cruise Sweepstakes was a natural extension of what makes Captain D’s special, which is bringing people together over great seafood and creating experiences that families can share,” said Phil Greifeld, CEO of Captain D’s. “Sandra’s story is exactly the kind of connection we hoped this promotion would create. She has been a Captain D’s guest for generations, and now she gets to experience Alaska with the people she loves most. We couldn’t be happier for her and her family.” The timing was especially meaningful for Elmore, just before she found out she won, Elmore was telling her husband how much she wanted to plan a family vacation with their two daughters and sons-in-law, but it was so difficult being in different states on different schedules. “Then the next week, I found out I’d won an Alaska cruise from Captain D’s,” Elmore exclaimed. “It was like my wish came true! It was truly amazing! Everyone is so excited!” That longtime connection made the news of her win even more special. For Elmore, Captain D’s has long been a wholesome family meal and a source of familiar favorites, including the restaurant’s classic fish and fries, fish tenders, green beans and baked potatoes. “It is hard to beat just the original fish and fries,” she said. “That’s kind of my comfort food of just a fun thing to grab.” For Elmore, the trip will be a first. She has never visited Alaska and has never taken a cruise. The family is now looking toward next summer for their Alaska adventure, with Elmore particularly excited about seeing the Inside Passage and glaciers. The Captain will be waiting when she returns, with fresh wild caught fish from Alaska. The post Longtime Captain D’s Guest Wins Cruise Trip to Alaska appeared first on QSR Magazine .

Starbird is bringing its Positively Delicious Chicken to the Midwest with plans to open its first Chicago-area restaurant in St. Charles, Illinois. The upcoming opening marks a major milestone in the fast-growing chicken brand’s expansion into the Midwest and the first of five planned locations in partnership with Keystone Management Group. Known for its bold, globally inspired flavors and culinary-forward approach to fast-casual dining, Starbird brings a fresh, flavorful approach with high-quality ingredients and made-from-scratch preparation. Tenders are antibiotic-free and hand-breaded daily, vegetables are freshly chopped, beverages are made in-house, and sauces are prepared from scratch, including Starbird’s signature Star Sauce. Guests can look forward to a diverse menu of crispy chicken sandwiches, tenders, wings, wraps, salads, nuggets and more. The brand’s innovative take on classic chicken favorites continues to drive its expansion into new markets nationwide. The first restaurant will open on Oct. 19 at 845 S. Randall Rd. in St. Charles, Illinois, with additional locations throughout the Chicago area expected to follow under the multi-unit agreement. Development will be led by Keystone Management Group, whose industry experience aligns with Starbird’s strategy of partnering with established operators in high-growth markets. “We’re incredibly excited to open the doors and introduce Starbird to the St. Charles community,” said Melanie Bowling with Keystone Management Group. “From the beginning, we wanted this opening to be about more than bringing a new restaurant to the area. St. Charles and the surrounding communities have such a strong sense of local pride, and we’re looking forward to celebrating alongside our guests while finding a fun way to give back to the schools and students who make this community special.” Starbird identified Chicago as a strategic next step in its national expansion due to the market’s scale, strong food culture and long term growth potential. With nearly 10 million consumers in the nation’s third-largest DMA, the market offers an opportunity to build brand awareness in one of the country’s most influential dining destinations as the brand expands its footprint. The expansion also allows Starbird to establish a local presence in the community and build lasting connections with guests through its commitment to quality and hospitality. “Expanding into Chicago is an important milestone for the brand and another example of our disciplined approach to growth,” said Greg Levin, CEO of Starbird. “We’re focused on entering markets where we see long-term opportunity and partnering with operators who can help us grow while preserving the guest experience and operational standards that define Starbird.” The Chicago announcement follows Starbird’s recent expansion into Washington state, where the brand opened its first location in Seattle. Taco Cabana, a celebrated fast casual Mexican-inspired dining chain, is closing out an exciting year of menu innovation with the launch of its new Chicken Poblano lineup, featuring four limited-time creations that put a fresh spin on familiar favorites. Available starting October 21, the launch also introduces Loaded Elotes, a new menu platform inspired by Mexican street corn, and Lime Margarita Cheesecake, a citrus-forward addition to the dessert menu. Announced by Ulyses Camacho, President and Chief Operating Officer of Taco Cabana, the new lineup centers on tender shredded chicken seasoned with poblano peppers and fresh cilantro, bringing bold flavor to four distinct creations: Chicken Poblano Quesabirrias with Consommé, Chicken Poblano Double Crunch Pizza, Chicken Poblano Loaded Elote and Chicken Poblano Folded Quesadilla. “2026 has been an incredible year for Taco Cabana, and we wanted to close it out with a launch that brings something fresh and exciting to our guests,” said Ulyses Camacho, President and Chief Operating Officer of Taco Cabana. “Chicken Poblano gave us the opportunity to take one standout flavor and create four distinct experiences around it. I’m especially excited about the quesabirrias, which put a new spin on a familiar favorite and reflect the kind of menu innovation we strive for at Taco Cabana.” Leading the lineup, Chicken Poblano Quesabirrias with Consommé reimagines a popular Mexican favorite with tender Chicken Poblano, melted quesadilla cheese and three corn tortillas served with a rich, green consommé infused with the aromatic flavors of poblano peppers and fresh cilantro. The vibrant, savory broth adds an herbaceous dimension to every dip, creating a distinctive twist on the quesabirria experience. Taco Cabana is also giving its Double Crunch Pizza a fresh makeover. The Chicken Poblano Double Crunch Pizza features two layers of golden, crunchy tortillas filled with creamy refried beans and topped with Chicken Poblano, sour cream, shredded cheese and diced tomatoes. The launch also marks the debut of Loaded Elotes, a new platform inspired by the bold, craveable flavors of Mexican street corn. The first creation, Chicken Poblano Loaded Elote, layers sweet corn with Chicken Poblano, creamy street corn sauce and sour cream for a savory, satisfying combination. The new platform creates opportunities for future street corn-inspired menu innovations. Rounding out the Chicken Poblano lineup, the Folded Quesadilla pairs Chicken Poblano and melted shredded cheese inside a warm flour tortilla for a flavorful, handheld option. Guests can also finish their meal with Lime Margarita Cheesecake, featuring creamy cheesecake, a citrusy lime glaze swirl and a graham cracker crust. Throughout 2026, Taco Cabana has continued to explore new flavor combinations and fresh interpretations of Mexican-inspired favorites. The latest launch builds on that momentum while establishing Loaded Elotes as a platform for future menu creations. “Our team continues to challenge itself to bring fresh ideas and bold flavors to life, and this launch is a great example of that creativity,” Camacho added. “From reimagining a fan favorite to introducing an entirely new menu platform, we’re continuing to find new ways to excite our guests and give them more reasons to come back. We’re finishing the year with great momentum, and we’re just getting started.” The Chicken Poblano lineup, Loaded Elotes and Lime Margarita Cheesecake launch October 21, 2026, at participating Taco Cabana locations for a limited time. articles.title: Teriyaki Madness Announces Partnership with Zipline’s Drone Delivery Service
articles.titleKo: Teriyaki Madness Announces Partnership with Zipline’s Drone Delivery Service
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Teriyaki bowls incoming! Beginning Thursday, Oct. 15, Teriyaki Madness (TMAD) is teaming up with Zipline , the world’s largest autonomous delivery service, to fly orders straight to customers across the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex and Houston later this year. No traffic. No detours. Just huge bowls of awesomeness, taking the express route from wok to sky to doorstep. Zipline’s all electric drones are entirely autonomous and have zero-emissions, meaning fanatics can get their teriyaki fix faster while putting a little less pressure on the planet. Most orders arrive in less than five minutes. This certainly isn’t Zipline’s first flight. Since 2014, the company has flown more than 140 million autonomous miles and now completes a delivery somewhere in the world every 20 seconds. Its network was built to transport blood, medicine, and critical medical supplies to more than 5,000 hospitals and health centers — work that continues across Africa today. Zipline brought its precision, home-delivery technology to the United States in 2025, and now serves dozens of communities through partnerships including retailers like Walmart and a growing roster of restaurant brands. “Getting bowls to people faster has always been the mission, and at some point you run out of shortcuts on the ground,” said Jodi Boyce, chief marketing officer of Teriyaki Madness. “Zipline has more flight experience than anyone out there, so we knew our bowls were in good hands — or, really, in good drones.” The launch caps a busy year for a brand that has spent 2026 doubling down on what fanatics want most: bigger value, bolder flavors, and fewer reasons to settle. And now, there’s one less reason to wait. Whether it arrives by air or by hand, every TMAD bowl is still cooked to order with fresh ingredients, crave-worthy proteins, signature sauces, and portions that prove everything really is bigger in Texas. “Zipline brings customers the food they’re craving the fastest way possible,” said Emily Snyder, vice president of restaurant sales at Zipline. “With Teriyaki Madness’s focus on fresh, premium ingredients, Zipline can make sure those quality meals are delivered exactly as the restaurant intended.” Zipline delivery will be available to TMAD customers starting at the Denton location and quickly expanding to additional shops across the Lone Star State. The delivery process is fast and simple: a customer places an order in the Zipline app. Once the order is ready, Zipline’s drones autonomously retrieve it, and quietly fly it to the delivery destination. Upon arrival, the drone stays up to 300 feet in the air while a smaller pod containing the order descends to the ground on a tether. The pod gently places the order on the ground with precision, and can even deliver in high winds and bad weather conditions. After delivery, the drone flies back to charge for its next order. articles.title: Salad and Go’s CoFounder is Bringing the Bankrupt Chain Back to Life
articles.titleKo: Salad and Go’s CoFounder is Bringing the Bankrupt Chain Back to Life
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Salad and Go once had nearly 150 locations. Salad and Go may not be finished after all. Two months after filing for bankruptcy and shutting down its remaining 70 restaurants, the once-promising drive-thru salad chain is preparing for a comeback under the direction of one of its original creators. Daniel Patiño, the brand’s cofounder and longtime executive chef, has partnered with Arizona restaurateurs Mike Myers and Tom Misitano, cofounders of Hospitality First Concepts, to acquire Salad and Go’s intellectual property and begin rebuilding the business. The group has plans to reopen restaurants in Arizona and eventually pursue franchising. The transaction gives Patiño an opportunity to restore a concept that grew from a single Gilbert, Arizona, restaurant in 2013 to nearly 150 locations before an aggressive expansion strategy, mounting financial losses, and widespread closures brought the business to an abrupt end. “I just felt like, you know, it can’t end this way, like I have to find a way to keep this going,” Patiño told FOX 10 Phoenix . The new ownership group, operating through Beyond Salt and Pepper LLC, acquired Salad and Go’s name, trademarks, and recipes for $180,000, according to bankruptcy court documents reported by local TV stations Arizona’s Family and KTAR News . The group also secured a former Salad and Go restaurant in Gilbert for $1 and is pursuing another location in Mesa. READ MORE : Salad and Go Files for Bankruptcy, to Close All Restaurants Dutch Bros and 7 Brew to Battle for Salad and Go Locations 7 Brew Wins Auction for 73 Salad and Go Sites in $143 Million Deal Patiño told Arizona’s Family that he hopes to reopen the first restaurant within six weeks of approval. The partners plan to operate company-owned restaurants and eventually make franchises available nationwide, according to KTAR. Hospitality First Concepts already operates several Arizona restaurant and hospitality businesses, including The Hub Grill and Bar and Rusty Buckle Saloon. The comeback won’t necessarily recreate Salad and Go’s previous operating model. Patiño told Arizona’s Family that the new restaurants will prepare food on-site, marking a significant departure from the centralized production strategy that supported the chain’s earlier expansion. “Not happy with the chicken that we had before, transparently, right? But we’re going to be making everything in each location,” Patiño told the television station. The team is also considering the return of popular proteins, including steak and shrimp, and has confirmed that the brand’s lemonades will return. Patiño indicated that the initial focus will be on getting the menu and existing locations operating successfully before pursuing additional growth. The planned revival comes after one of the more dramatic collapses in recent quick-service history. Salad and Go built its reputation around compact, drive-thru-only restaurants serving affordable salads, wraps, breakfast burritos, and other nutritious meals. The concept attracted attention for its ability to offer freshly prepared food at prices competitive with traditional fast-food chains. But the company’s expansion into Texas and Oklahoma proved difficult. Salad and Go invested in a large commissary kitchen in Garland, Texas, capable of supplying as many as 500 restaurants within a 12-hour drive. Problems involving site selection, brand awareness, and its centralized production model contributed to financial pressure as the chain expanded. The company began closing restaurants in September 2025, announcing 41 closures across Texas and other markets. Another 32 followed in January 2026 as Salad and Go abandoned Texas and Oklahoma entirely. Those cuts left 70 restaurants in Arizona and Nevada, down from more than 140 in May 2025. articles.title: KFC U.S. Announces New Beverage Partnership with Coca-Cola
articles.titleKo: KFC U.S. Announces New Beverage Partnership with Coca-Cola
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The partnership marks another significant milestone in KFC's broader Kentucky Fried Comeback. KFC U.S. on Thursday announced a new partnership with The Coca-Cola Company, another step in the brand’s ongoing effort to refresh its menu and beverage platform and create more reasons for customers to visit. Beginning in January 2027, KFC will transition its U.S. beverage partnership to The Coca-Cola Company, with Coca-Cola products expected to be served in all U.S. restaurants by spring 2027. “I’m incredibly excited to bring KFC and Coca-Cola together. These are two originals, with deep consumer love” said Catherine Tan-Gillespie, President of KFC U.S. “This partnership is about more than what’s in the cup. It is another step in our work to evolve KFC, strengthen our restaurants, menu offerings and create a more relevant experience for today’s customers. Coca-Cola shares our ambition for the future of this brand, and I’m excited about what we can create together.” “This exciting new partnership brings Coca-Cola and KFC together across the U.S. for the first time,” said Dagmar Boggs, President of Foodservice & On-Premise, North America, The Coca-Cola Company. “By pairing KFC’s iconic food and flavors with the breadth of Coca-Cola’s beverage portfolio and innovation capabilities, we have an incredible opportunity to make every visit more refreshing, create memorable consumer experiences and unlock new growth possibilities together.” The partnership will bring together KFC’s signature food and Coca-Cola’s broad beverage portfolio to create compelling food-and-drink pairings, expand choice and explore new ways to make the KFC experience more complete. Together, the two brands see an opportunity to serve customers across more occasions, whether they are gathering over a family meal, stopping in for a snack or looking for something refreshing on its own. Coca-Cola’s extensive system capabilities will also support KFC restaurants across the U.S. The announcement comes as KFC continues to evolve its beverage platform through new drink offerings, expanded daypart occasions and innovation already underway across several global markets. Recent examples include the new drink lineup introduced at Open House, the brand’s new innovation restaurant in McKinney, Texas, featuring iced coffees, boba, shakes and other craveable creations designed to give fans more flavor and more reasons to visit. Together, the new Coca-Cola partnership and KFC’s continued expansion of beverages mark the next step in KFC’s plan to meet changing consumer preferences and create a more relevant customer experience. The partnership brings two iconic originals together as part of the broader Kentucky Fried Comeback, with a shared ambition to build memorable experiences around great food and beverages. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Smalls Sliders, the industry-disrupting cheeseburger slider brand, has signed a multi-unit development agreement to bring four Cans to Florida’s Atlantic Coast, further expanding the brand’s footprint across high-growth markets in the state. Seasoned entrepreneurs Joe Sloboda and Stanley Tsung of Stacked Hospitality will lead the development. Sloboda and Tsung bring decades of combined experience developing and operating multi-unit restaurant concepts across Florida and internationally. The duo has successfully grown franchise brands throughout Florida, Brazil, and Taiwan, building a strong track record of identifying high-potential concepts and introducing them to new markets. Smalls Sliders will become the fourth concept they have brought to South Florida. The group plans to develop four Cans across a territory spanning Florida’s Space Coast to as far south as Jensen Beach and throughout the Treasure Coast. Sloboda and Tsung expect to open their first Can in Port St. Lucie, marking Smalls Sliders’ debut in the region. “South Florida is a dynamic market with communities that embrace convenient, high-quality dining concepts, making it a strong fit for Smalls Sliders,” said Sloboda. “We see tremendous potential to build a meaningful presence here and introduce more guests to the brand’s unique experience. As we grow, our focus will be on becoming part of the communities we serve and creating Cans that people are eager to visit again and again.” Sloboda has called South Florida home since the early 1980s, while Tsung established roots in the region after immigrating from Brazil to Fort Lauderdale in 2014. Together, their ties to the area give them a strong connection to the communities where they plan to grow. The Stacked Hospitality partners will take an active role in developing and operating each Can, pairing their local market knowledge with Smalls Sliders’ craveable menu and streamlined operating model. Together, they aim to establish Smalls Sliders as a go-to burger destination along Florida’s Atlantic Coast. “Florida continues to play an important role in Smalls Sliders’ growth story, and expanding along the Atlantic Coast is a natural next step for the brand,” said Richard Leveille, Vice President of Franchise Development for Smalls Sliders. “Joe and Stanley bring extensive operating experience and a strong understanding of the communities they plan to serve.
